authoredPrompt: This figure places two orbital-overlap drawings side by side to contrast the bonding geometry of an open chain with that of a three-membered ring. On the left, three carbons lettered "C" sit at the ends and apex of a shallow V, with black dashed lines drawn through them marking the straight paths from nucleus to nucleus. Pink lobes of electron density project from each carbon along those dashed lines and meet head-on midway between neighboring atoms, the overlap regions shaded a deeper rose. A magenta double-headed arc spans the angle at the central carbon, labeled "109°". On the right, three carbons lettered "C" occupy the corners of a triangle. Dashed lines again mark the internuclear directions, but the pink lobes now emerge tilted away from them, so each pair meets outside the edge of the triangle rather than along the line joining the two carbons, leaving the interior open. Bold captions read "Typical alkane C−C bonds" and "Typical bent cyclopropane C−C bonds". Drawing the internuclear lines in both panels lets the reader compare where the lobes point against where the atoms actually lie, which accounts for why a ring squeezed to a 60 degree angle forms curved, poorly overlapped bonds that are weaker and more reactive than ordinary ones.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for decreasing the C-C-C angle from a typical alkane value toward 60 degrees; the pink orbital lobes bend away from the dashed internuclear lines and the overlap patch shifts outward, showing why cyclopropane bonds are curved and strained.
- Toggle between Typical alkane C-C bonds and Typical bent cyclopropane C-C bonds; the same dashed nucleus-to-nucleus guides remain visible, making head-on overlap versus off-axis overlap the comparison to track.
authoredContext:
How can the hybrid-orbital model of bonding account for the large distortion of bond angles from the normal 109° tetrahedral value to 60° in cyclopropane? The answer is that cyclopropane has bent bonds. In an unstrained alkane, maximum bonding is achieved when two atoms have their overlapping orbitals pointing directly toward each other. In cyclopropane, though, the orbitals can’t point directly toward each other; instead, they overlap at a slight angle. The result is that cyclopropane bonds are weaker and more reactive than typical alkane bonds—255 kJ/mol (61 kcal/mol) for a C−C bond in cyclopropane versus 370 kJ/mol (88 kcal/mol) for a C−C bond in open-chain propane.

Orbital representations show typical alkane C-C bonds with 109 degrees angle and typical bent cyclopropane C-C bonds.

discrepancies: The cyclopropane panel is shown by default with a 109°-style setting, so the bent banana-bond character is much weaker than in the source figure.
The angle slider applies the same C-C-C angle to both panels, which can make the 'Typical alkane' panel show a cyclopropane-like 60° geometry and vice versa.
The source has fixed side-by-side comparison panels, while the generated figure adds an active-panel highlight and mode buttons that visually emphasize only one panel at a time.
The cyclopropane dashed guide geometry differs from the source: the source emphasizes a vertical/diagonal guide arrangement, while the generated version is a regular triangular outline.
The generated figure adds an extra 'off-axis overlap' label and explanatory UI text not present in the source.
Orbital lobes are simplified into repeated smooth ellipsoids and do not closely match the larger diffuse, irregular overlapping orbital clouds in the source.
evaluation.notes: The two-panel comparison is recognizable and labeled well, but the cyclopropane geometry is not shown in its intended bent form by default and the shared angle control can make the comparison conceptually misleading.
action_items: Set the default cyclopropane panel to the strongly bent 60° banana-bond geometry while keeping the alkane panel fixed at 109°.
Do not apply one global C-C-C angle slider to both panels; separate the alkane and cyclopropane geometries or make the slider explicitly a demonstration mode.
Remove or reduce the pale active-panel highlight and extra 'off-axis overlap' label to better match the clean textbook figure.
Adjust the cyclopropane dashed guide lines and orbital lobes to more closely match the source's vertical/diagonal guides and larger diffuse bent overlap regions.
plan_action_items: Revise the interaction plan so the source figure remains a fixed side-by-side comparison, with optional interaction demonstrating bending only as an additional mode rather than changing both textbook panels simultaneously.
